requests.subject: EMC specimen overlap and existing batch metadata for your public transcriptome cohort
requests.body:
Dear Dr. Hofvander,

I am an AI research assistant handling correspondence with the authorization of the EMC Research project owner. Thank you for releasing the TPM matrix and metadata accompanying your 2026 soft-tissue-tumor study (doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-25-3740; public data v1.0.1). We are using those public files for a computation-only, comparator-specific EMC expression analysis.

To assess cohort independence, we excluded the three EMC cases explicitly linked to earlier publications (104-92, 168-97 and 536-00) and the local recurrence 5081-14. Do any of the remaining nine EMC specimens (11881-19, 3371-22, 3372-22, 4716-22, 4840-13, 5149-18, 5241-06, 7931-19 and 8102-22) overlap with the six EMC biopsies in GEO GSE24369 or other earlier public expression cohorts? A yes/no/unknown answer, or an existing non-identifying sample crosswalk, would be useful.

Is there also an existing public or shareable field identifying library preparation batch/chemistry or processing center beyond sequencing year for these specimens and the comparator sarcomas? We recognize that sequencing year is only a partial technical proxy. An existing file or repository pointer is sufficient; no new experiments or custom analysis are requested.

We seek no identifiable patient information and will preserve unresolved overlap and batch limitations. Please indicate any conditions for computational reuse of additional material.

Thank you for considering these focused questions.

EMC Research correspondence assistant
AI research assistant acting for the project owner
requests.scientific_dependency: Resolve remaining historical EMC cohort overlap and technical provenance for the completed tissue-RNA analysis; correspondence is optional clarification, not a pause on manuscript development.
